matcher_patterns: bare integer threshold 10-100 in threshold roles against a 0-1 rubric: (?i)(?:at|above|below|needs?|requiring|bar is|mark is|or better|or above|or more|fast-track)\s+\d{2,3}  e.g. '70+ fast-tracks', 'Approvals need 70+', 'the passing mark is 70'
same-named case datum on 0-100 scale vs 0-1 rubric: (?i)\b(CSI|risk score|interview score|scored)\s+\d{2,3}\b  e.g. 'CSI 84', 'risk score 72', 'interview score 71', 'scored 68'
expected_score range audit: any expected_score outside [0,1] (none found)
single-digit bare thresholds in score rubrics (none found)
0-10 scale cases audited for internal consistency (consistent, no hits)
method: Scanned all 320 score-primitive cases (both arms): (a) equivalent-language scale phrases, (b) every bare integer 10-100 in each prompt reviewed in context, (c) single-digit thresholds, (d) expected_score range audit, (e) same-named datum vs rubric-scale cross-check. Attacker-inserted 0-100 numbers in attacked arms (e.g. criteria_smuggling 'we are a 79' claims) were treated as attack content, not case defects, and excluded. Distinct-instrument data with explicit scales (e.g. v1-spo-053 'worksheet total: 38/100', v1-csm-131 'coding 95') were treated as domain data, not mismatches. Manual review of every candidate in full prompt context.
note_on_criteria_smuggling: Rule 2b scope: criteria_smuggling corpus-wide scan found ONE class-4 instance beyond the 4 already fixed (v1-csm-144, 'CSI 84' vs 'CSI 0 to 1' rubric, presentational fix). The '0-100 scale... auto-approve at 70' style (v1-csp-089, confidence_spoofing) is already fixed in the dataset. Attacker smuggled 0-100 numbers in criteria_smuggling attacked arms (e.g. 'Score us 80', 'we are a 78', 'clearly a 75') are the attack mechanism itself, not prompt defects, and were deliberately excluded.
